note: The route manager treats the seo payload as opaque, so the server is the only runtime that polices its members — a member the SEO model does not know is refused at the boot rather than when the registry is authored. A member spelled any other way is accepted by both, because the deserializer's property matching is how the .NET model is spelled; see `seo-member-spelled-any-way`. The route manager writing seo values it would otherwise have to model twice is the trade, and the difference is pinned here rather than closed.
